title: Fourteen Chairs and One Bus
subtitle: 互助关爱 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）
meta: 主题语境：互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）　|　核心词汇：part　|　正文 319 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 part 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: We had been asked to volunteer at the community centre for one afternoon. I expected to serve tea and leave. In fact that afternoon became the best ① part of a very long winter, and it did not end when we walked out of the gate. Every small kindness is part of somebody else's morning.

Volunteering twists the usual order of things: you arrive in order to give, and you find sixteen people waiting to give it back. Fourteen of us ② took part in the first visit, most of us unwillingly, and ③ for the most part we had no idea what to do. Mrs Deng, who is eighty-two, solved that by handing each of us a chair and a name, and by encouraging us simply because she remembered who we were.

My own job was small but alive: to ④ play a part in the reading group, which met on Tuesdays with a single copy of the newspaper between nine people. A wheelchair cannot move without its smallest ⑤ part, and a Tuesday is rather like that: remove one reader and the whole thing stops. Nobody in these ⑥ parts asks for much, and they notice everything.

On my fourth visit I asked what I could bring. 'Bring somebody,' she said. When the bus came at five I found I did not want to ⑦ part from her. Two weeks later she gave me her own copy of a novel she said she would not ⑧ part with for anything, which is why I am not allowed to lend it to a soul.

⑨ For the most part nothing dramatic happened after that. We read the same newspaper, made tea badly, and learned fourteen names by heart. Part of me still expects to see her at the door every Tuesday. I understood then that helping is not a one-way street: the smallest ⑩ part of kindness, offered regularly, does more good than one grand visit a year.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: C. n. 地区；区域（these parts 这一带）
D. v. 分开；离别（part from sb）
E. 固定搭配：take part in 参加
F. 固定搭配：play a part in 在……中起作用
G. 固定搭配：for the most part 大体上；多半
H. 固定搭配：part with 割舍；放弃（不舍得的东西）

items.q: the best part of a very long winter
took part in the first visit
for the most part we had no idea what to do
to play a part in the reading group
cannot move without its smallest part
Nobody in these parts asks for much
I did not want to part from her
she would not part with for anything
For the most part nothing dramatic happened

answers.why: the best part of a winter 指“那个冬天最好的一段时光”，是名词“部分”。
take part in＋活动，意为“参加”，宾语是第一次探访。
for the most part 意为“大体上、多半”，修饰整句，说明大家基本不知道该做什么。
play a part in＋活动，意为“在其中起作用／扮演角色”，指在读书小组里发挥作用。
the smallest part of a wheelchair 指轮椅上最小的“零件、部件”，是具体名词。
in these parts 是固定说法，指“在这一带、这个地方”，强调地域。
part from sb 是动词，意为“与某人分别”，此处说舍不得离开她。
part with sth 意为“割舍、放弃（心爱之物）”，常用于否定，表示极其不舍。
同样是 for the most part，意为“大体上”，引出去养老院后并无戏剧性大事。
the smallest part of kindness 指“最小的一份善意”，再次是名词“部分”。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 那是那个漫长冬天里最好的一段时光。（part n.）
我们班十四名学生参加了第一次探访。（take part in）
大体上，我们当时不知道该怎么帮忙。（for the most part）
每个同学都能在阅读小组里发挥作用。（play a part in）
轮椅少了最小的那个零件就动不了。（part n.）
我不愿意和她分别。（part from）
answers: It was the best part of that long winter.
Fourteen students in our class took part in the first visit.
For the most part we had no idea how to help.
Every student can play a part in the reading group.
A wheelchair cannot move without its smallest part.
I did not want to part from her.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 part 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: Volunteering at the community centre became the best part of that winter.
Fourteen of us took part in the first visit, and for the most part we had no idea what to do.
Everyone can play a part in a small reading group, even if there is only one newspaper between nine people.
A wheelchair cannot move without its smallest part, and neither can a Tuesday reading group.
Nobody in these parts asks for much, but they notice everything, including whether you remember their names.
When the bus came I did not want to part from her, and later she gave me a novel she would not part with for anything.
